fact_basis.fact: SECURE 2.0 section 604 makes optional the treatment of employer matching/nonelective contributions as Roth; the contribution must be nonforfeitable (vested) when received; it is not excludable from gross income
fact_basis.source: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/n-24-02.pdf (Notice 2024-2, Part L, "Section 604 of the SECURE 2.0 Act")

fact_basis.fact: Page text: "Since the SECURE 2.0 Act (2022), employers can now offer Roth matching — some companies have updated their plans... Check with your HR department."

actions.task: Reword heading/body so it reads: match is pre-tax by default; since SECURE 2.0 a plan may (not must) let you take vested match money as Roth, taxed in the year allocated. Tell reader to check the plan document or HR. Fix the table row the same way. No new figures.

actions.q: When can I withdraw Roth 401(k) money tax-free?

fact_basis.fact: A qualified distribution is generally one made after a 5-taxable-year period of participation and either on/after age 59½, after death, or due to disability; the 5-year period ends when five consecutive taxable years have passed, starting the first day of the taxable year of the first designated Roth contribution

A nonqualified distribution includes the earnings portion in gross income; the tax-free basis portion is the distribution times the ratio of Roth contributions to total account balance (IRS example: $5,000 from $9,400 contributions + $600 earnings = $4,700 tax-free, $300 taxable)

actions.task: New FAQ: tax-free only if the 5-year period is met AND age 59½/death/disability; otherwise earnings share is taxable pro rata (use the IRS $5,000 example or a simple ratio sentence). Practical tone; do not state a 10% penalty figure unless sourced (omit it).
